title: 7. Conflict Between Fundamental Rights and DPSP

blocks.content:
Initially, Fundamental Rights were given more importance over DPSP.
Current position:
• Both should be harmoniously interpreted.
• Parliament can amend Fundamental Rights to implement DPSP.
Important Case Reference:
• Kesavananda Bharati Case – Doctrine of Basic Structure.

rows: Fundamental Rights were given more importance over DPSP
DPSP could not easily override Fundamental Rights
Parliament can amend Fundamental Rights to implement DPSP

items: The Kesavananda Bharati Case is frequently asked in relation to the Doctrine of Basic Structure.
Exams often test the current legal position regarding the relationship between FRs and DPSPs (Harmonious Construction).
Note that Parliament can amend Fundamental Rights specifically to implement DPSP.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Initially, Fundamental Rights were accorded primacy over Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP).
The current position requires that Fundamental Rights and DPSPs must be harmoniously interpreted.
Parliament retains the power to amend Fundamental Rights in order to implement DPSP.
The Kesavananda Bharati Case established the Doctrine of Basic Structure.
